text:
Vladislav Gavrikov's best moment this month may have come away from the rink: Mollie Walker of the New York Post wrote about his adventure game show debut back in Russia, a show he told her he watched "every single weekend" growing up. On the ice it's been tougher. He's pointless in seven straight games, and our numbers say that one isn't just luck: the chances have thinned out too.

He's still a big-minute defenceman, about 21 and a half a night beside Adam Fox on the top pair, and the Rangers take 54% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there. That's fine, not special. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, though it also found he was better than his goals (0.7 expected wins against -0.7 actual), so the finishing or goaltending behind him let him down. His shooting this year (3.6%) will come up. A 14-goal season like last year's looks unlikely; our range centres on about eight.
